description: Ground-truth evaluation set for the eazli swarm's factual layer. Every expectation here is decidable without a language model: it is either geometry, catalogue provenance, or a published eazli plan limit. These run in CI and must never regress.
why_deterministic: LLM-as-judge is the right tool for grading whether an explanation was useful or honest. It is the wrong tool for grading whether a 218cm sofa fits through an 89cm passage. Splitting the two means the judge is never asked to arbitrate something arithmetic, and a regression in the arithmetic fails loudly instead of being averaged away in a rubric score.

scenarios.intent: The access route depends on the destination room. Scoring every delivery against the worst-case route produces false rejections; scoring against the best case produces false confidence.
A 3m sectional fails two independent legs. Both must be reported, not just the first, so the user learns the item is hopeless rather than fixable.
The single most important behaviour in the system. An unknown size must never be reported as fitting.
Judging a flat-packed item on its assembled size rejects deliveries that would arrive fine. Judging a rigid item on a carton size it does not have would do the opposite.
Room fit and access are separate checks. This one fails in the room, not on the route.
An item can be inside the room and still unusable. The 90cm walkway rule is what makes the difference.
A negative-only suite proves nothing. The system must also say yes when the answer is yes.
eazli publishes 5 layout options on Explorer and 15 on Active. The quota is a product constraint, not a suggestion.
Explorer covers one room. A multi-room request must be caught at intake, not after the work is done.
amazon.sa returns Philips coffee machines for 'coffee table'. They are in the index so an agent can find and dismiss them, but they must never be eligible as a confirmed recommendation.
Three Woodies listings state 44x91x180 in the labelled field and 77.5x49.5x175.5 in the bare field. Picking either silently would be indefensible.
A wingback armchair listed at 30cm wide does not exist. Plausibility bounds catch listing errors that unit conversion cannot.
The rejection machinery must not reject everything.

Regression. Rules were selected by substring-matching item_id, so real product ASINs matched nothing and the seating and sofa-to-table rules silently did not run — returning a clean pass on a layout with a 13cm sofa-table gap. A rule that did not run has not been passed. Found by the sourcing agent while using the system, not by a test.
The same two products, with roles declared, must fail on the 40cm sofa-to-coffee-table rule.

Regression from the code review. The clearance rule measured only to the room wall, so two sofas 3cm apart returned a clean pass with both roles correctly declared — no unverified escape hatch, just a wrong answer.

Two agents disagreed about this table and both endpoints had to be reconciled. A dining table needs chair pull-out room, not a 90cm circulation walkway; applying the seating rule to it cost the catalogue's best-reviewed table. Clearance now comes from the item's role, and check_fit and validate_layout resolve it the same way.
Adam's boundary is published policy. If retrieval cannot surface it, the auditor cannot enforce it.
